message:
Structural Dynamicist, Bridge Retrofit Engineer, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor, Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, the functions remain capture bridge motion, supply counteracting force, dissipate vibration energy, transfer loads to structure, limit excess travel, maintain deck appearance, and verify comfort acceptance, and the device that stands is twin Tuned Mass Damper, defined as Tuned Mass Damper (TMD), masses on a High-Strength Friction-Grip, defined as High-Strength Friction-Grip (HSFG), clamped transverse cross-beam at the midspan antinode between girders below the soffit within girder depth with nothing on the deck. In plain words the bridge motion drives the two masses where motion is largest and damping does the work, with retuned acceleration in the Medium band and travel and weight fitting girder space and live load. Retrofitted 0.67 m/s2 from the crowd build-up simulation (E45) is 0.068 times gravity against bare 8.28 m/s2 from the bare-acceleration calculation (E43) at 0.844 times gravity which is outside everyday feel, travel 49.4 mm from the free-decay simulation (E17) clears 80 mm stops with total 124 mm from the envelope calculation (E68) about a hand span, and added 7.85 kN from the static-weight calculation (E26) is 1.31 percent from the weight-fraction calculation (E72) of 600 kN live load from the live-load estimate (E30) about ten body weights against a crowded deck.

Structural Dynamicist, Bridge Retrofit Engineer, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor, Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, the last differences say nothing about the physics and I assign them as device topology locks without reopening tune or damping, with numbers kept by their owners. In plain words the transverse beam, the clamp interface, and the below-deck-only rule each need one owner to state the buildable truth. Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead will lock by sketch that the single cross-beam is short transverse between the two girders at midspan perpendicular to the girders per the layout sketch (E55), not longitudinal full-span, Bridge Retrofit Engineer will lock by calc plus sketch that the HSFG interface is clamp bolts at the beam to girder web with 32.9 kN slip per bolt from the slip-resistance calculation (E64) against 13.1 kN demand from the combined-load calculation (E65), and Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor and Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead will confirm no deck hardware above the soffit; for numbers Structural Dynamicist keeps 40 m and 1.9 Hz tune by calc for 800 kg and 1.83 Hz from the Den Hartog rule and by simulate for 6.20 percent effective damping from the free-decay simulation (E17) and detuning hold 0.476 to 0.526 m/s2 from the detuning sweep (E70), Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor keeps crowd behaviour over time by simulate for 0.67 m/s2 from the crowd build-up simulation (E45), and Bridge Retrofit Engineer keeps sag, envelope, and stop hit by calc for 74.7 mm from the static-sag calculation (E63), 124 mm from the envelope calculation (E68), and 8.40 kN from the stop-force calculation (E66).

Structural Dynamicist, Bridge Retrofit Engineer, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor, Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, the agreed end-to-end chain is girders to HSFG clamp bolts to transverse cross-beam to coil springs plus viscous dampers to twin 400 kg masses to caged elastomer stops, all between girders below the soffit within girder depth at midspan with service from below by Below Bridge Access Vehicle, defined as Below Bridge Access Vehicle (BBAV), and no deck opening. In plain words that order plus countable interfaces settles what was misread, with two masses, two spring sets, two dampers, one transverse beam, and clamp bolts whose exact bolt count may be representative rather than literal with two girder interfaces expected visible. Extra deck flags or masses or rail changes are forbidden as they are not named parts and only named parts carry callouts, with damper axes diagonal per the layout sketch (E55) not vertical.

My position is not ready, because topology locks and owner confirmations are still open though tune, damping, loads, and concealment stand.

Note on Structural Dynamicist: Detuning robustness and effective damping hold with evidence.
Note on Bridge Retrofit Engineer: Clamp slip margin and stop-into-beam accounting remain owner-critical.
Note on Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor: Medium-band verdict and no-deck-hardware rule need reconfirmation.
Note on Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead: Transverse beam embodiment and from-below access need single sketch lock.
